outcome: mode of delivery (specifically assisted perineal lateral incisions)
premature rupture of membranes (incidence and duration)
congenital heart disease (specifically atrial septal defect)
duration of enteral and intravenous nutrition during hospitalization
cohort: The study included 144 twin preterm infants (72 conceived via IVF and 72 naturally conceived) born between January 2021 and June 2024 at a single hospital and transferred to its neonatal unit.
finding: IVF twin preterm infants exhibited significant differences in clinical characteristics and maternal perinatal disorders, including higher incidences of assisted perineal lateral incisions, premature rupture of membranes, atrial septal defect, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, intracranial hypertension syndrome, and hypocalcemia, but a lower incidence of twin-twin transfusion syndrome, compared to naturally conceived twin preterm infants.
mod_finding: The IVF group had a significantly higher proportion of assisted perineal lateral incisions compared to the naturally conceived group.
followup_time: until discharge from the neonatal unit
